intro: Malmö is Sweden's third city, at the southern tip of the country across the Öresund from Copenhagen. In Magistratsparken, a small city park in Rådmansvången, grows a weeping beech whose hanging branches have built a three-peaked green dome on the lawn, the trunk only visible from underneath. A reader sent us its photograph and calls it majestic. We do not yet know its age or girth.

trees.name: The Weeping Beech of Magistratsparken
trees.story:
"Majestic Hängbok," wrote the reader who sent us this tree from Magistratsparken in Malmö, and the photograph bears the word out. Hängbok is Swedish for weeping beech, Fagus sylvatica 'Pendula', the form of the common European beech whose branches turn down instead of up.

This one has had a lawn to itself long enough to become a building of leaves. Its crown rises in three green peaks, like a small range of hills, and from every limb the branches pour straight down in curtains until they hang just above the grass, so that from the path it reads less as a tree than as a single green mass. Only underneath, in the shade, does the trunk show, short and dark, carrying the whole weight. Benches line the path along the edge of the crown.

Magistratsparken is a small city park in Rådmansvången, close to Malmö Konsthall and the city theatre. We do not know when the beech was planted, how big round its trunk is, or how old it might be. If you know, or have measured it, tell us here and we will add it with your figures.

Our pin marks the park, not the tree. Come in summer and walk right round it on the lawn, and watch the dome change shape with every step.
